summary.title: Understanding the Power of Bitwise Operators. No math needed
summary.one_liner: Bitwise operators (&, |, ~, ^, <<, >>) manipulate the binary representation of data using masks, and they power practical tasks such as decoding instructions in a Chip-8 emulator.
keywords: shift by power of 2 multiply divide
takeaways: Bitwise AND with a mask keeps or clears selected bits; OR sets bits; XOR toggles bits; NOT (~) flips all bits to build masks.
Left shift by n multiplies by 2^n and right shift divides by 2^n, with zeros filled in on the open side.
Hexadecimal is a compact way to write binary, with one hex digit per 4 bits, which makes masks easier to read.
Chip-8 instruction decoding uses masks like 0xF000, 0x0FFF, 0x0F00 and shifts by 8 and 4 to extract opcode fields and register indexes.
Windows, Linux and macOS calculators have programmer modes that show binary and hex conversions, useful for experimenting.
summary.summary: The author explains bitwise operators from the ground up, starting with bits, nibbles, bytes and words, then covering AND, OR, invert, XOR and shifts through worked binary examples built around masks. It introduces hexadecimal notation and suggests using a programmer calculator to practise conversions. The final section applies these ideas to a Chip-8 emulator, showing how masks and shifts decode 16-bit instructions and pick out register operands. The tone is informal and beginner-friendly, with the math kept minimal.
